rationale: B wins because it keeps the real three stories and refuses to pad the set. Its governance angle, "The reader is the admin who has to decide whether to let software write to production records," has an actual buyer, beat, risk, and proof path. A is good until it gets greedy with "employees are the ones left to catch what they get wrong," which turns an absence of reliability data into an invented workplace experience. That is how a decent angle set walks itself into a reporter's follow-up trap.
gaps_in_A: "employees are the ones left to catch what they get wrong" invents the operating model. The update says reliability data is undisclosed, not that employees are the fallback control system.

"Airtable's new AI agents will draft your emails and update your records" is too close to the governance/reliability angle; the worker lens needs a real employee source or workflow detail to stop being a costume change.

"enterprise AI agents are now trustworthy enough to act autonomously on production data" overstates the prevailing belief. The update supports a trust question, not a fully established industry premise.

"All four angles are blocked on the same gaps" is sloppy triage. The valuation angle needs valuation timing and investor color; the governance angle needs reliability and controls; the category angle needs positioning proof and an executive. Different holes, different fixes.
gaps_in_B: "widely known product" is a small outside assumption. It is likely true, but the supplied update only says Airtable serves many enterprise teams.

"rebuilds itself around AI agents" is a shade hotter than the fact pattern. The update supports a repositioning and agent launch; do not make it sound like the whole company has already structurally transformed.

The category angle asks for "one enterprise team, named" even though the brief says named customers are not disclosed. Fine as a proof requirement, but it should be flagged as a blocker, not treated like normal prep.

It skips the employee-experience lens entirely. That was probably the right call without a worker source, but it is still a potential angle once Airtable can show what humans see, approve, reverse, or clean up.
